title: How AI Makes Pictures
about: How AI turns random speckles into a picture that fits your words.

cards.title: A cat astronaut, in seconds
cards.body:
Type "a cat in a space suit, floating past the Moon, as a watercolour" into an image tool, and seconds later there it is. Nobody drew it.

AI that makes new things (pictures, text, music, voices) is called **generative AI**. Chatbots are one kind; image tools are another.

cards.prompt: An image model learned from captioned pictures. Match each word in a picture [[prompt]] to what it changes.

pairs.right: How many things are in it

cards.hint: Think about what each word would change if you were painting it yourself.
cards.nudge: Pick out the camera word and the time-of-day word first: what does each change?
cards.explanation: Style words (**watercolour**) change how it's painted, time words (**at sunset**) the light, camera words (**close-up**) how near it seems, and numbers (**two cats**) what's in it.

cards.prompt: Image tools start from **random static** and clear it step by step: colour, then shapes, then detail. Order the stages.
cards.hint: Speckles come first and the finished picture last. The middle follows the prompt's order.
cards.nudge: Big, rough things come before fine things. Which stage is only colour, with no shapes?
cards.explanation: It starts from **random static**, then clears to **blobs of colour**, **rough shapes** and **details**, until the **finished picture**.

cards.prompt: You type the **exact same** prompt into an image tool twice. What will you most likely get?

options.text: The same picture twice, because computers are exact
options.nudge: Each picture starts from new random static. What does that do to the result?

options.text: A better one the second time: it learned from the first
options.nudge: It doesn't learn from your pictures. What changes between the two tries?

options.text: Two different pictures that both match your words
A message saying it has already made that picture
options.nudge: It doesn't keep track like that. What does each picture start from?

cards.hint: Think of every picture's first stage. Is it ever the same twice?
cards.explanation: Each picture starts from **different random static**, so you get **two different pictures**, both matching your words.

cards.prompt: AI pictures **sometimes** have give-aways that real photos rarely do. Is each a **possible clue**, or **not a clue**?

items.label: A sign with jumbled, unreadable letters
A shadow going the wrong way
A dark photo taken at night

cards.hint: Which of these happen in ordinary photos taken with a phone?
cards.nudge: Which of these rarely happen in real photos?
cards.explanation: Jumbled letters, six fingers and wrong-way shadows **rarely happen in real photos**: possible clues, not proof. Blur, filters and night shots are normal in real photos.

cards.prompt: You check a picture carefully: normal hands, readable signs, shadows all fine. What can you conclude?

options.text: It's real, because AI pictures always have mistakes
options.nudge: AI pictures sometimes have give-aways, but lots don't. Does finding none prove anything?

options.text: It's AI, because a picture with no flaws is too perfect
options.nudge: Real photos are often flawless too. Can "no mistakes" prove it either way?

options.text: It's from an older AI tool that didn't make mistakes
options.nudge: Older tools made more mistakes, not fewer. What does finding none tell you?

options.text: Nothing for sure: good AI pictures often look flawless

cards.hint: Newer tools make fewer give-aways. So what does **not** spotting one tell you?
cards.explanation: Lots of AI pictures have no give-aways, and neither do real photos, so "no mistakes" proves **nothing either way**. Check where it came from instead.

cards.prompt: Nobody gave an image model rules about paint. How did it learn what "watercolour" looks like?

options.text: It searches for a watercolour each time, and copies it
options.nudge: It makes a new picture, not a copy. Where did it learn the style?

options.text: From many captioned watercolours in its training data
It cuts up saved watercolours and mixes the pieces
options.nudge: It keeps no pictures to cut up: it learned a pattern. From where?

options.text: Someone wrote rules for every watercolour brush stroke
options.nudge: Rules versus learning: could anyone write rules for every brush stroke?

cards.hint: Think back to what an image model learned from, and what came with each picture.
cards.explanation: It saw lots of pictures **captioned** as watercolours and learned the pattern. It makes a **new** picture from static, rather than copying or cutting up saved ones.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Image models learned from millions of captioned pictures.
- They clear random static step by step, so pictures differ.
- Give-aways are clues, but finding none proves nothing.

Next: fake voices and faces.
